analysis.title: GS Basics - China Restrictions. 2018 Playbook. FCI Tight.
key_insights: Equities liquidated sharply from the US open on 11/19 with SPX reversing 3.3% intraday, despite catalysts the author expected to be supportive. The author calls it a violent liquidation and says the cause is unclear.

New BIS chip export rules, effective November 19 and directed by Treasury and the NSC, restrict direct chip sales to China and also specified advanced compute accessed remotely by Chinese entities through overseas data centers. The author reads this as an attempt to close the offshore compute loophole, with substantial overlap with the proposed RASA legislation.

China faces pressure on three fronts: direct access to advanced chips, remote access to overseas compute, and its ability to manufacture leading-edge technology under tighter restrictions on overseas foundries.

The author sees the most immediate issue as uncertainty over who can access what and under which licensing regime, not permanent loss of Chinese demand. That uncertainty could freeze incremental investment decisions. The author says this partly explains the weakness in the Asian data center trade, alongside broader China weakness and the Shanghai market testing its lows.

The author lists four existing drivers of lower AI multiples: cost of capital (further challenged by a change of leadership at NVDA), data center restrictions, oversupply and efficiency gains for inference, and lack of revenue to support capex.

Technicals were poor: bearish high/low close, SPX took out virtually every reasonable support area, and breadth was 38 S&P constituents advancing against 464 declining. Negative gamma into expiry likely amplified the move.

The defensive bid failed. Utilities and staples sold off with everything else despite lower Treasury yields. They still outperformed relatively, but offered no absolute protection. The author says a rolling rotation increasingly looks like outright equity liquidation.

Financial conditions have tightened very quickly. Waller's 50bp comments helped shock the market, and Fed speakers this week were mostly hawkish. The author sees the November/December 2018 parallels as increasingly close, with the Fed at risk of overtightening into a market already under stress.

2yr inflation breakevens have collapsed toward their lows while 2yr real yields are near relative highs, a large tightening in real policy conditions. The long end may be starting to price a policy mistake, with yields and breakevens falling while equities and gold liquidate.
The author sees a shift from an inflation problem to a growth and liquidity problem, and thinks the market pivots when central banks pivot.

Most investors are in risk reduction mode. The author says a technical component such as forced funding or liquidation may not repeat, but breaking this many charts across this many assets is inconsistent with a bull market tape.

Receiving rates and owning duration is the one trade the author sees as misaligned with equity internals and still relatively attractive. Gold is an important coincidental indicator, showing liquidation in reaction to real rates and FCI.

Contrarian view: the depth of pessimism and one-sided de-grossing suggest the market may be approaching a tactical local low. Catalysts are scarce: PCE next Wednesday, NFP, and the December FOMC. November CPI is seen as the next major anchor and potentially the one that forces a Fed recalibration.

tension_points.bull_case: The depth of pessimism and one-sided de-grossing suggest the market may be approaching a tactical local low, and some of the selling may have been forced funding or liquidation that will not repeat.
tension_points.bear_case: Breaking this many charts across this many assets, with failed defensives and tighter financial conditions, is inconsistent with a bull market tape, and the Fed risks overtightening as in late 2018.
tension_points.what_invalidates: November CPI is the next major anchor and could force a Fed recalibration. The report gives no price level.
